card.title: Understand the Hurt
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I texted that I'd lost my job. You replied, 'What's for dinner?'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought something normal would help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Making your dinner? Can you see why I felt like the cook?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant we could go out. I'll book somewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I believe you. Before you book, can you see why I heard a chore? I needed you to ask how I was.

mechanism: A asks B to understand why an ordinary dinner reply after job loss felt like assigning a chore rather than giving care.
confusable: Unlike disputing B's intention, A must secure recognition of the reason the words hurt.
comparison: D99-b accepts the intended meal out while pausing for acknowledgment; D99-a accepts possible lateness while explaining irreplaceable presence.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
